subproblem.title: Line slices of the Steiner symmetral have the length of the slices of A
subproblem.statement: Let d ∈ ℕ, j ∈ Fin d and let A ⊆ ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be compact. For x ∈ ℝ^d and s ∈ ℝ let x[j↦s] be x with its j-th coordinate replaced by s (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s)). Let A^j_x := {s ∈ ℝ : x[j↦s] ∈ A} and S_j(A) := {x ∈ ℝ^d : A^j_x ≠ ∅ and |x_j| ≤ (L¹(A^j_x)).toReal/2}. Then for every y ∈ ℝ^d, L¹({t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)}) = L¹(A^j_y), where L¹ is the volume (Lebesgue measure) of ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d : ℕ) (j : Fin d) (A : Set (Euclid d)), IsCompact A → ∀ y : Euclid d, volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ {x : Euclid d | {s : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s) ∈ A}.Nonempty ∧ |x j| ≤ (volume {s : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s) ∈ A}).toReal / 2}} = volume {t : ℝ | WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update y.ofLp j t) ∈ A}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3, 4 and 5 of the parent proof of cbr_ci_iso_steiner_volume_eq, written for the line through an arbitrary point y ∈ ℝ^d instead of the fibre over z (Simon Ch. 1, proof of 2.10: S_j(A) meets each line ℓ_j(ξ) that meets A in the closed segment {|t| ≤ ½ L¹(A ∩ ℓ_j(ξ))}). Notation: x[j↦s] := WithLp.toLp 2 (Function.update x.ofLp j s), A^j_x := {s ∈ ℝ : x[j↦s] ∈ A}, x_j := x.ofLp j. Fix y ∈ ℝ^d and put B := A^j_y, ℓ := (L¹(B)).toReal ≥ 0 and F := {t ∈ ℝ : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)}. We must show L¹(F) = L¹(B).
1. Coordinate identities. For t ∈ ℝ, (y[j↦t]).ofLp = Function.update y.ofLp j t (WithLp.ofLp_toLp), so (y[j↦t])_j = Function.update y.ofLp j t j = t (Function.update_self). For t, s ∈ ℝ, Function.update (Function.update y.ofLp j t) j s = Function.update y.ofLp j s (Function.update_idem), so (y[j↦t])[j↦s] = y[j↦s]. Consequently A^j_{y[j↦t]} = {s : y[j↦s] ∈ A} = B for every t ∈ ℝ.
2. Description of F. By the definition of S_j(A), t ∈ F iff A^j_{y[j↦t]} ≠ ∅ and |(y[j↦t])_j| ≤ (L¹(A^j_{y[j↦t]})).toReal/2. By step 1 this condition reads: B ≠ ∅ and |t| ≤ ℓ/2. So F = {t ∈ ℝ : B ≠ ∅ ∧ |t| ≤ ℓ/2}.
3. L¹(B) < ∞. The coordinate map π : ℝ^d → ℝ, π(x) := x_j, is continuous, so π(A) is compact (IsCompact.image) and L¹(π(A)) < ∞ (IsCompact.measure_lt_top). If t ∈ B, then x := y[j↦t] ∈ A and π(x) = t by step 1. Thus B ⊆ π(A), and L¹(B) < ∞ by measure_lt_top_of_subset.
4. Case B = ∅. No t satisfies the condition of step 2, so F = ∅ and L¹(F) = 0 = L¹(∅) = L¹(B).
5. Case B ≠ ∅. Then F = {t : |t| ≤ ℓ/2} = [−ℓ/2, ℓ/2] (abs_le). By Real.volume_Icc, L¹(F) = ofReal(ℓ/2 − (−ℓ/2)) = ofReal(ℓ) = ofReal((L¹(B)).toReal). This equals L¹(B) by ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, which applies because L¹(B) ≠ ∞ by step 3. (When ℓ = 0, F = {0} and both sides are 0.)
6. In both cases L¹({t : y[j↦t] ∈ S_j(A)}) = L¹(F) = L¹(B) = L¹(A^j_y). Since y ∈ ℝ^d was arbitrary, the claim holds for every y. ∎
proof_key_steps: (y[j↦t])_j = t and (y[j↦t])[j↦s] = y[j↦s] (WithLp.ofLp_toLp, Function.update_self, Function.update_idem), so A^j_{y[j↦t]} = A^j_y =: B for every t.
B is contained in the compact image π_j(A), so L¹(B) < ∞.
If B = ∅ both measures are 0. Otherwise the set is Icc (−ℓ/2) (ℓ/2), whose measure is ofReal ℓ = L¹(B) (Real.volume_Icc, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).

audit.reason: The one-line Lean proposition exactly matches the compactness hypothesis, symmetral definition, and universally quantified slice equality. Repeated coordinate updates leave the original slice unchanged. Its inclusion in the compact coordinate projection proves finite measure, justifying ENNReal.ofReal_toReal. The proof separately handles empty slices and nonempty centred intervals, including zero-length slices. No global measurability assumption on the symmetral is needed for this calculation. The supplied proof is complete and independent of the parent and sibling; the empty dependency list is correct, and the frozen type and isolated proof compile.
